dedupe_keys.name: grdc global runoff database river discharge

description: The Global Runoff Database is the largest quality-assured collection of in-situ river discharge data at global scale, held by the Global Runoff Data Centre at Germany's Federal Institute of Hydrology under the auspices of the World Meteorological Organization. Established in 1988 to support research on global change and integrated water resources management, it gathers daily and monthly discharge series from national hydrological services. The GRDC Data Portal lets users search and visualise stations on a map or table, select them by station, country, region or one of 841 hydrographic subregions, and request a download in several export formats, with watershed boundaries of stations as geospatial add-ons. Summary tables list stations, record lengths and earliest and latest years by country, WMO region and basin. Access is free of charge but identified: a form must be completed and a download link is emailed. The data policy forbids commercial use and redistribution, and data ownership stays with the providers. Caveats: station density and recency vary strongly; for some countries the series end decades ago (Afghanistan in 1980, Algeria in 2003), so the database is uneven for recent events. Simulation uses: calibrating and validating hydrological and flood models that drive dam operation, flood defence and water supply scenarios, characterising low flows for drinking water and irrigation abstraction, and testing hazard exposure under climate change. Related records: global flood forecasting systems such as GloFAS use in-situ discharge like this for evaluation.
